raw_response:
I have farmed this 6.5 mu in Quzhou for 50 years, and at 72 I still make every decision myself. I finished high school and later took county extension courses, so I understand soil fertility and nutrient balance better than most. My land is heavy loam with decent organic matter, but after decades of wheat-maize rotation the phosphorus is medium-high and potassium is adequate. With only me in the household now, I hire two workers for wheat harvest and maize sowing season, but I do the spraying and fertilizing myself.

For winter wheat this year: I will plant the improved variety Jimai 22 at 12.5 kg per mu. Before sowing in mid-October I will spread 50 kg per mu of compound fertilizer, the 15-15-15 grade from the cooperative. That gives me 7.5 kg nitrogen, 7.5 kg phosphate, and 7.5 kg potash per mu as base. At green-up in late March I will topdress 18 kg per mu of urea, and at jointing in mid-April I will add another 12 kg per mu of urea. Total nitrogen comes to about 16 kg per mu — I could push to 18 kg but urea is 2.4 yuan per kg now and I need to save cash for maize season. I will irrigate four times: winter irrigation after sowing, green-up, jointing, and grain filling. I will spray herbicide once before winter, and at heading I will spray fungicide for powdery mildew mixed with insecticide for aphids — three pesticide applications total. I will do rotary tillage before wheat sowing to break up the maize stubble. My target is 550 kg per mu.

For summer maize: After wheat harvest in early June I have maybe five days to plant before I lose yield potential. I will plant Zhengdan 958 hybrid seed at 2.5 kg per mu. I will use no-tillage direct seeding into the wheat stubble because June heat dries the soil fast and my well has limited flow. I will band 40 kg per mu of 15-15-15 compound fertilizer at sowing, then at big trumpet stage I will spread 25 kg per mu of urea. That gives me about 19 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphate, and 6 kg potash per mu. I will irrigate three times: at seedling if it does not rain, at tasseling — which is the most critical stage you cannot miss — and at grain filling. I will spray herbicide once at the 3-leaf stage and corn borer insecticide once at heart leaf stage — two pesticide applications total. My expected yield is 600 kg per mu.

I watch my neighbors closely. Old Wang across the road puts 14 kg nitrogen on his wheat and gets 500 kg per mu. I prefer to spend 50 yuan more per mu on fertilizer and sleep better. A failed crop means I lose my entire year's income; wasting 20 kg of urea is just a cost I can absorb on 6.5 mu.
